doc.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Moments in history he wishes he had heard
summary: He names Jelly Roll, Red Allen, Charlie Parker, Coltrane, and Miles at the Plugged Nickel, and Wes Montgomery.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: This could be a question you might need to think about, but if you could be a fly on the wall and go back in history, are there any moments that you wish you could have witnessed?

Oh I would have like to have heard Jelly Roll live. That would be great. I found that, you know when I started listening I was listening to only the avante garde or what was considered the avante garde then. And now there is some traditional jazz, or the early classics, and I still don’t feel like I understand and know how they are — I mean they give me a lot of joy to listen to Jelly Roll or the Hot Fives. And that’s just as big a mystery to me as the Art Ensemble was when I first started listening to the Art Ensemble. So I would really like to have heard those. Red Allen is somebody I would have loved to have heard live during the thirties. I would have liked to have been on the recording session where Coleman Hawkins, Red Allen and Waymon Carver did the first flute solo on “Sweet Sue.” That would have been fun for me. Oh what else? I try — I’m more

curious about what’s going to happen basically than what’s already happened. I would have like to have heard Charlie Parker live. That would have been great. I think I heard Charlie Parker when I was about two or three, on the radio. I think that was really like my first early memory of hearing a saxophone solo. And as much as I can recapture it now, I think it must have been Bird. I can’t imagine who else it would have been. I heard Coltrane live. I guess I would like to revisit that because it was way over my head when I heard it. And actually Dave Liebman is going to give me a tape of that concert so I will get a chance to hear it again. I stood outside The Plugged Nickel when Miles was there with Wayne Shorter, Tony Williams, Ron Carter and Herbie. And I would have liked to have been able to go inside. I was too young to go inside.
Yeah. But I would have enjoyed that I think too. And Wes Montgomery. I wish I had caught the Half Note with Wynton Kelly. I would have really dug that.
